paraphrase: Liberation while living (jīvanmukti) is impossible: while the body lasts, karma and bondage remain, and scripture places release after the body falls; the Advaitin's 'liberated-while-living' is still bound.
speaker: Vedānta Deśika

paraphrase: Following the ancient path seen by Yatirāja (Rāmānuja), or resorting to a doctrine close to it, O wise ones, reciting this (work) as it has been stated, like parrots, strive on every side for victory over the crypto-Buddhists (pracchanna-bauddha).

original.text: प्राचीमुपेत्य पदवीं यतिराजदृष्टां तत्सन्निकृष्टमपि वा मतमाश्रयन्तः । प्राज्ञा यथोदितमिदं शुकवत्पठन्तः प्रच्छन्नबौद्धविजये परितो यतध्वम्
original.edition: as quoted in the editor's introduction to Vedānta Deśika's Nyāyapariśuddhi (eBhāratī-sampat), which states that the Śatadūṣaṇī announces this at its head ('tadgranthamukha eva')
original.licence: eBhāratī-sampat — quotation for reference with attribution

speaker: Vedānta Deśika
notes: Verse verified only as quoted by the modern editor; its position among the Śatadūṣaṇī's opening verses not checked.
